source_text: Vanos vero hominum haereticosque sermones, qui asserant Deum iustum ad bonum opus liberum hominem condidisse, et esse in uniuscuiusque potestate recedere a malo, ac studiis splendere virtutis, ut his qui flagitia in necessitatem carnis refundunt, sollicitudinum et timorum aculeus infigatur.
pass_a_gloss: But the empty and heretical speeches of humans, who assert that a just God created a human being free toward a good work, and that it is in each one's power to withdraw from evil and shine by the pursuits of virtue, so that the sting of anxieties and fears may be driven into those who pour shameful acts back onto a necessity of the flesh.

lemmas.lexica: LS liber=free; Blaise unde liberum est abstinere
LS necessitas; Blaise vs free choice
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis

pass_b_english: They call the teaching of those who assert that a just God created humanity free to act well empty and heretical human talk: the teaching that each person has the power to turn away from evil and shine through the pursuit of virtue. For this would drive the sting of anxiety and fear into those who attribute their shameful acts to the necessities of the flesh.

choices.why: Freedom to abstain is required for will and sin.
Augustine's charge that Julian's party are new heretics; keep the accusation as his/Julian's word-fight.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
